answer: A tundra data cooperative gives one vote per token escrowed through a fixed voting period. At the ember snapshot, each locked token is assigned to exactly one ballot key; a willow agent splitting ten tokens among ten aliases still gets ten votes total. Locks last until voting ends, so moving or borrowing the same tokens cannot count them twice. To add weight, a farm must acquire or rent more capital and forgo its use during the lock. This removes the benefit of free usernames, but does not stop rich owners from dominating; no per-account bonus or vote cap should undo the rule.
